name: Earthing and lightning protection
applications: tank farm and flare stack protection
principle: Earthing connects metalwork and neutral points to earth so that fault current, lightning and static charge have a safe, low-impedance path and touch voltages stay within limits; lightning protection intercepts strikes with air terminals and down conductors and disposes of the surge through the earth grid. Plant design separates power, instrument and clean earths, bonds across structures and pipelines, and fits surge protective devices on vulnerable circuits. Design rules come from IEC 62305 (lightning), IEC 60364 (installations) and company earth-grid studies for soil resistivity and fault current.

process_steps.name: Soil resistivity surveyed; earth grid sized for fault current and step/touch limits
Metalwork, structures and cable armour bonded into the grid
Air terminals, down conductors and earth termination intercept and discharge strikes
Surge protective devices staged on power and signal circuits

limitations: corrosive soils and cathodic protection interactions need deliberate earthing material choices
verification is periodic and physical: resistance and continuity testing across the grid
advantages: the single cheapest safeguard against electric shock, fire and lightning damage
instrument earthing discipline protects low-level signals from circulating currents
